text:
maria: Hey team, getting intermittent 403s from our prod app hitting /v1/generate since yesterday evening. Request ID: req-20260317-9a1b. Body says "signature_mismatch".

maria: Quick curl I used to repro locally:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_XXXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: req-20260317-9a1b' \n  --data '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hello world","policy":"a+b"}'
```

ana: thanks for the report — can you confirm the exact token type (org key vs project key) and the org_id on the request? also please paste the full response body (redact secrets).

maria: response body:
```json
{"error":"signature_mismatch","message":"computed signature != header","request_id":"req-20260317-9a1b"}
```
org_id on our side: org_789, token was sk_proj_XXXXX (project-scoped).

ana: copying in @kevin (oncall) and @dmitri (eng) — looks like a signature mismatch rather than a policy permission denied.

kevin: quick checks: 1) is the client URL-encoding the body differently ("a+b" can become "a%2Bb")? 2) which signing lib/version are you using? we had a regression in the v1.2.0 signer where plus signs in policy got normalized.

maria: our stack uses ruby-sign-1.2.0 (from bundle). that might be it.

dmitri: okay that matches the known bug. can you also run the debug collector and attach the bundle? command for customer debug is: `rw-debug collect --request req-20260317-9a1b --include-headers --include-replay` — this will grab the raw signed string we received.

maria: uploaded bundle to https://internal-uploads.company/bugs/1797501234.tar.gz (shared).

deploy-bot: log snippet for req-20260317-9a1b: `recv_signature=abc123, computed_signature=def456, reason=payload-normalization-mismatch`

kevin: looking at the bundle — the client sent policy as literal `a+b` but the canonicalized payload our verifier used was `a%2Bb` (percent-encoded). verifier and signer differ on normalization.

kevin: short-term workaround: switch to an org-scoped key (sk_org_...) or escape policy on the client side with percent-encoding. longer-term we'll patch ruby-signer and release v1.2.1.

ana: maria — can you try one of these repros for us so we can mark the case as triaged? 1) re-sign with percent-encoded policy; or 2) rotate to an org-scoped key and retry. also include the exact curl you run and the response.

maria: tried percent-encoding in curl, now returns 200. repro curl I ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_XXXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: req-20260317-9a1b-2' \n  --data '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hello world","policy":"a%2Bb"}'
```

maria: note: rotating to org key also fixed it for a minute but we reverted because of scoping differences (project-level limits).

dmitri: thanks — that confirms signer normalization mismatch. i'll open a patch ticket against ruby-signer and add a test for plus/percent handling. ETA for patch: end of day.

ana: I'll keep the support case updated and advise customers to apply the client-side workaround or rotate to org key if feasible. tagging as P2.

maria: appreciated, thanks everyone :heart:
